description: S-parameter data handling and visualization, network parameter conversion, RF circuit and link budget analysis, and antenna element design, analysis and array modelling.

tools.name: sparameters
tools.description: Create an S-parameter object from a Touchstone file, from raw data, or by analysing an RF circuit or antenna. It stores the scattering matrix over frequency together with the reference impedance and provides methods for extraction, deembedding and conversion. It is the central data type of RF Toolbox.
tools.usage:
sobj = sparameters(filename)
sobj = sparameters(data, freq)
sobj = sparameters(data, freq, z0)
sobj = sparameters(circuitObject, freq)
s21 = rfparam(sobj, 2, 1)

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Touchstone file path: .s1p, .s2p, .s4p and so on.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: N-by-N-by-numFreq array of complex S-parameters.

parameters.name: freq
parameters.description: Frequency vector in Hz.

parameters.name: z0
parameters.description: Reference impedance in ohms (default 50).

tools.notes: yparameters, zparameters and abcdparameters create the corresponding network-parameter objects.

tools.name: rfplot
tools.description: Plot the magnitude in dB of selected S-parameters against frequency, with automatic labelling and legends. Called with no port arguments it plots every S-parameter in the object. It is the quickest way to inspect a measured or simulated network.
tools.usage:
rfplot(sobj)
rfplot(sobj, i, j)
rfplot(sobj, i, j, lineSpec)
rfplot(sobj, 'abs')
hLines = rfplot(___)

parameters.name: sobj
parameters.description: An S-parameter (or other network parameter) object.

parameters.name: i, j
parameters.description: Output and input port indices to plot.

parameters.name: plotType
parameters.description: 'db' (default), 'abs' or 'angle'.

parameters.name: lineSpec
parameters.description: Standard line style specification.

tools.example:
S = sparameters('passive.s2p');
figure
rfplot(S, 1, 1, '-r')
hold on
rfplot(S, 2, 1, '--b')
legend('S_{11}', 'S_{21}')
grid on
figure, rfplot(S)    % everything at once

tools.name: smithplot
tools.description: Display reflection coefficients on a Smith chart, the standard polar representation of complex impedance normalized to the reference impedance. Matching network design and impedance trajectory analysis are done directly on this chart. Data tips report the impedance, VSWR and return loss at any marker.
tools.usage:
smithplot(sobj)
smithplot(sobj, i, j)
smithplot(freq, gamma)
h = smithplot(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: sobj
parameters.description: S-parameter object.

parameters.name: i, j
parameters.description: Port indices of the reflection coefficient to plot.

parameters.name: gamma
parameters.description: Complex reflection coefficient values, as an alternative to an object.

parameters.name: 'TitleTop' / 'LegendLabels' / 'GridType'
parameters.description: Chart appearance options.

tools.name: s2y
tools.description: Convert scattering parameters to admittance (Y) parameters for a given reference impedance. Y-parameters are the natural form for combining networks in parallel and for extracting shunt element values. The conversion is exact and works for any number of ports.

parameters.name: s_params
parameters.description: N-by-N-by-M array of S-parameters.

parameters.name: z0
parameters.description: Reference impedance in ohms (default 50).

tools.notes: The related conversions are s2z, s2abcd, s2h, y2s, z2s and abcd2s.

tools.name: s2z
tools.description: Convert scattering parameters to impedance (Z) parameters for a given reference impedance. Z-parameters are the natural form for combining networks in series and for extracting series element values. The conversion assumes the ports are all referenced to the same impedance unless a vector is supplied.
tools.usage:
z_params = s2z(s_params)
z_params = s2z(s_params, z0)
z_params = s2z(s_params, z0, portImpedanceType)

parameters.name: s_params
parameters.description: N-by-N-by-M array of S-parameters.

parameters.name: z0
parameters.description: Reference impedance, scalar or per port.

parameters.name: portImpedanceType
parameters.description: 'power' (default) or 'voltage' wave definition.

tools.name: rationalfit
tools.description: Fit a rational function model to frequency-domain data such as measured S-parameters, giving a compact pole-residue representation. The fitted model can be evaluated at any frequency, converted to a time-domain impulse response, and exported for circuit simulation. Enforcing passivity and stability is essential when the model will be used in a transient simulation.
tools.usage:
fit = rationalfit(freq, data)
fit = rationalfit(freq, data, tol)
fit = rationalfit(___, Name, Value)
resp = freqresp(fit, freq)
[y, t] = timeresp(fit, u, ts)

parameters.name: freq, data
parameters.description: Frequency vector and the complex response to fit.

parameters.name: tol
parameters.description: Relative error tolerance in dB (default -40).

parameters.name: 'NPoles'
parameters.description: Number of poles, or a [min max] range to search.

parameters.name: 'IterationLimit' / 'DelayFactor'
parameters.description: Fitting effort and delay extraction control.

parameters.name: 'TendsToZero'
parameters.description: Logical; force the response to vanish at infinite frequency.

tools.name: rfbudget
tools.description: Compute a cascaded RF chain budget, reporting gain, noise figure, OIP3, output power and SNR at every stage. Elements are ordered from input to output and can be amplifiers, mixers, filters or S-parameter blocks. It is the standard first-pass analysis for a receiver or transmitter line-up.
tools.usage:
rfb = rfbudget(elements, inputFrequency, inputPower, bandwidth)
rfb = rfbudget(Name, Value)
show(rfb)
rfbudgetAnalyzer(rfb)
sobj = sparameters(rfb)

parameters.name: elements
parameters.description: Array of RF elements: amplifier, modulator, nport, rffilter, txrxsite and so on.

parameters.name: inputFrequency
parameters.description: Input carrier frequency in Hz.

parameters.name: inputPower
parameters.description: Available input power in dBm.

parameters.name: bandwidth
parameters.description: Signal bandwidth in Hz, used for the noise calculation.

parameters.name: 'AutoUpdate'
parameters.description: Logical; recompute automatically when elements change.

tools.name: circuit
tools.description: Build an RF circuit from lumped and distributed elements connected by named nodes, then extract its network parameters over frequency. Elements such as resistor, capacitor, inductor, nport and txline are added with the add method and wired by node numbers. Use it to design and analyse matching networks and filters.
tools.usage:
ckt = circuit
ckt = circuit(name)
add(ckt, nodes, element)
setports(ckt, [p1 gnd], [p2 gnd])
S = sparameters(ckt, freq)
show(ckt)

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.description: Two-element node vector giving where the element connects.

parameters.name: element
parameters.description: resistor, capacitor, inductor, nport, txline, or another circuit.

parameters.name: setports
parameters.description: Defines which node pairs are the external ports.

tools.name: rfckt.cascade
tools.description: Model a chain of RF components connected in cascade using the legacy rfckt object system. Each stage can be an amplifier, mixer, transmission line, LC filter or imported S-parameter data. Analyse the chain over frequency with the analyze method and plot the results.
tools.usage:
casc = rfckt.cascade('Ckts', {c1, c2, ...})
analyze(casc, freq)
plot(casc, 'S21', 'dB')
s = sparameters(casc, freq)

parameters.name: 'Ckts'
parameters.description: Cell array of rfckt objects in signal order.

parameters.name: analyze
parameters.description: Method that computes the network parameters over the supplied frequency vector.

parameters.name: plot / smith / polar
parameters.description: Visualization methods for the analysed results.

tools.notes: The newer circuit/nport and rfbudget objects are preferred for new work; rfckt remains for legacy compatibility.

tools.name: dipole
tools.description: Create a strip dipole antenna element whose length, width, feed gap and tilt are all settable properties. Its methods compute impedance, S-parameters, radiation pattern, current distribution and efficiency using a method-of-moments solver. A half-wave dipole is the standard reference element for antenna work.
tools.usage:
d = dipole
d = dipole(Name, Value)
show(d)
Z = impedance(d, freq)
pattern(d, freq)
mesh(d, 'MaxEdgeLength', len)

parameters.name: 'Length'
parameters.description: Dipole length in metres; about half a wavelength for resonance.

parameters.name: 'Width'
parameters.description: Strip width in metres; wider gives a broader bandwidth.

parameters.name: 'FeedOffset'
parameters.description: Feed position relative to the centre.

parameters.name: 'Tilt' / 'TiltAxis'
parameters.description: Orientation of the element in space.

tools.name: patchMicrostrip
tools.description: Create a rectangular microstrip patch antenna on a dielectric substrate, with configurable patch dimensions, ground plane, substrate properties and feed position. Patch antennas are low profile, cheap to fabricate and dominate GPS, Wi-Fi and satellite terminals. Use design to size it automatically for a target frequency.
tools.usage:
p = patchMicrostrip
p = patchMicrostrip(Name, Value)
p = design(patchMicrostrip, freq)
show(p)
pattern(p, freq)
S = sparameters(p, freqVector)

parameters.name: 'Length' / 'Width'
parameters.description: Patch dimensions in metres.

parameters.name: 'Height'
parameters.description: Substrate thickness.

parameters.name: 'Substrate'
parameters.description: A dielectric object, e.g. dielectric('FR4') or dielectric('Teflon').

parameters.name: 'GroundPlaneLength' / 'GroundPlaneWidth'
parameters.description: Ground plane size.

parameters.name: 'FeedOffset'
parameters.description: [x y] feed point offset, which sets the input impedance.

tools.name: linearArray
tools.description: Build a uniform linear array of identical antenna elements with a specified spacing, amplitude taper and phase taper. Varying the phase taper steers the beam electronically and the amplitude taper controls sidelobe level. Pattern, impedance and correlation analyses work exactly as for a single element.
tools.usage:
arr = linearArray
arr = linearArray(Name, Value)
pattern(arr, freq)
show(arr)
beamwidth(arr, freq, 0, 0:1:359)

parameters.name: 'Element'
parameters.description: The antenna element to replicate, e.g. dipole or patchMicrostrip.

parameters.name: 'NumElements'
parameters.description: Number of elements in the array.

parameters.name: 'ElementSpacing'
parameters.description: Centre-to-centre spacing in metres; half a wavelength avoids grating lobes.

parameters.name: 'AmplitudeTaper'
parameters.description: Per-element excitation magnitudes, e.g. a Taylor or Chebyshev window.

parameters.name: 'PhaseShift'
parameters.description: Per-element phase in degrees, used for beam steering.

tools.notes: rectangularArray and conformalArray build 2-D and arbitrary-geometry arrays.

tools.name: design
tools.description: Automatically size an antenna or array for a specified resonant frequency, returning a new object with all dimensions scaled appropriately. It saves you from working out wavelength-dependent dimensions by hand for every element type. An optional impedance argument targets a particular feed impedance for some element types.
tools.usage:
ant = design(antennaObject, frequency)
ant = design(antennaObject, frequency, Z0)
arr = design(arrayObject, frequency)

parameters.name: antennaObject
parameters.description: A template antenna or array object such as patchMicrostrip or helix.

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.description: Target operating frequency in Hz.

parameters.name: Z0
parameters.description: Target feed impedance in ohms, where the element supports it.

tools.name: pattern
tools.description: Compute and plot the radiation pattern of an antenna or array, in 3-D or as 2-D azimuth and elevation cuts. Pattern types include directivity, gain, realized gain, efficiency and the individual field components. With output arguments it returns the pattern data for further processing.
tools.usage:
pattern(antenna, frequency)
pattern(antenna, frequency, azimuth, elevation)
[patternData, azOut, elOut] = pattern(___)
pattern(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.description: Analysis frequency in Hz.

parameters.name: azimuth, elevation
parameters.description: Angle vectors in degrees; supplying one as a scalar gives a 2-D cut.

parameters.name: 'Type'
parameters.description: 'directivity' (default), 'gain', 'realizedgain', 'efficiency', 'power', 'powerdb'.

parameters.name: 'CoordinateSystem'
parameters.description: 'polar' (default), 'rectangular' or 'uv'.

parameters.name: 'Polarization'
parameters.description: 'all' (default), 'H', 'V', 'RHCP', 'LHCP'.

tools.name: impedance
tools.description: Compute the input impedance of an antenna over frequency, returning the complex value or plotting resistance and reactance against frequency. The resonant frequency is where the reactance crosses zero, and the resistance there sets the matching requirement. It is the primary analysis for tuning an element.
tools.usage:
Z = impedance(antenna, frequency)
impedance(antenna, frequency)
[Z, Gamma] = impedance(___)

parameters.name: antenna
parameters.description: An antenna or array object.

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.description: Scalar or vector of frequencies in Hz.

tools.notes: returnLoss and vswr give the matching performance directly against a reference impedance.

tools.name: show
tools.description: Display the 3-D geometry of an antenna, array or circuit, colour-coding the conductors, dielectrics and feed points. Viewing the geometry is the quickest check that dimensions and orientation are what you intended. It also reveals whether the element has been meshed yet.

parameters.name: antenna / array
parameters.description: Any Antenna Toolbox element or array object.

parameters.name: circuitObject
parameters.description: An RF Toolbox circuit or rfbudget object, shown as a schematic.
